p01.why: A braced list is not an operand of the comma operator.

p02.why: i++ completes before i * 10, so r is 20.

p03.why: An array bound asks for a constant expression, so the comma operator must be in parentheses.

p04.why: The overloaded comma evaluates its left operand before its right operand, so the log is l then r.

p05.why: The cast to void marks the left operand as intended, so -Wunused-value does not warn.

p06.why: The parenthesized comma is a valid template argument with the value 2, and step() gives 10 in constant evaluation.

p07.why: The result has the value category of x, so it is an lvalue for & and int&, and an xvalue for int&&; r = 6 sets x.

p08.why: The loop ends with i 3 and j 7; k becomes 1 and the while loop stops at 5.

p09.why: Both temporaries live to the end of the full expression and are destroyed in reverse order, giving 1, 2, -2, -1, 9.

p10.why: Parenthesized comma operators give a = 5, b = 6, and s.x = 2; the declarators p and q are separate.

p11.why: The right operand is not converted, so (0, cells) is an int[10] lvalue and (0, act) is a function lvalue.

p12.why: A case label asks for a constant expression, so case 1, 2 is not valid.

p13.why: a() runs first, then b(), and r gets 20.

p14.why: count(1, 2) has two arguments; count((1, 2)) has one argument, the value 2.

p15.why: The parenthesized comma operator gives the index 2.

p16.why: a + 1 has no effect, so -Wunused-value warns and -Werror makes it an error.

p17.why: b = (2, 3) gives 3, and the initializer list {1, 2} has two elements.

p18.why: With a void right operand the built-in comma applies, so used stays 0; (Tag{}, 2) calls the overload and returns 7.

p19.why: The left operand can be void, and the result is 4.

p20.why: The comma operator is allowed in a constant expression and gives 2.

p21.why: In parentheses the comma operator is a valid array bound with the value 2.

p22.why: A top-level comma in a subscript separates two arguments, and the built-in subscript takes one.

p23.why: (x, y) is an int lvalue and (x, 3.0) is a double prvalue, so (x, y) = 9 sets y.

p24.why: a becomes 1 then 3, so r is 30.
